syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Company introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793 and how it defined the zamindar's role.
Analyse why zamindars repeatedly failed to pay the fixed revenue demand in the early decades of the Permanent Settlement.

topics.title: The rise of the jotedars and the resistance of zamindars

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how jotedars consolidated their power in the villages and undermined zamindari authority.
Explain the strategies, such as fictitious sales, by which zamindars retained control of their estates.
Explain why and how the Fifth Report on the East India Company's administration came to be prepared in 1813.
Evaluate the limitations of the Fifth Report as evidence for the history of rural Bengal.

topics.title: The Paharias of the Rajmahal hills

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the forest-based livelihood and shifting cultivation of the Paharias.
Analyse the relations of the Paharias with plains people and the British, from raids to pacification.
Explain how and why the Santhals were settled in the Damin-i-Koh and how their settlements expanded.
Explain the causes and consequences of the Santhal Revolt of 1855-56.
Explain how Buchanan's surveys served the commercial interests of the East India Company.
Interpret Buchanan's descriptions to evaluate his idea of progress and its conflict with forest dwellers' lives.

topics.title: A revolt in the Bombay Deccan and the ryotwari system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the course and pattern of the 1875 revolt of the Deccan ryots against sahukars.
Explain the ryotwari settlement and the Ricardian ideas behind it.
Explain how high revenue demand, falling prices and famine pushed Deccan peasants into debt.

topics.title: Cotton boom, credit crisis and the Deccan Riots Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the American Civil War created a cotton boom in the Deccan and how credit dried up after it.
Analyse how moneylenders violated customary norms and used bonds and laws against the ryots.
Evaluate the Deccan Riots Commission report as an official source on peasant unrest.

chapters.title: Rebels and the Raj: The Revolt of 1857 and Its Representations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the common sequence of actions through which mutinies broke out and widened into a rebellion in 1857.
Interpret the evidence of communication, planning and collective decision-making among the sepoys.
Explain how pre-British rulers and local leaders came to lead the revolt in different regions.
Identify the rumour about the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle.
Recall the other rumours, prophecies and omens such as the Plassey centenary prophecy and the chapattis.
Analyse why rumours spread in the context of British reform policies, annexations and missionary activity.
Explain the stages of the British takeover of Awadh from the Subsidiary Alliance of 1801 to annexation in 1856.
Analyse how the disarming of taluqdars and the Summary Settlement of 1856 turned taluqdars and peasants against British rule.
Explain the links between sepoy grievances and the rural world of Awadh.
Evaluate the limits of sources on the rebel viewpoint and interpret rebel proclamations such as the Azamgarh Proclamation.
Explain how rebel proclamations appealed to Hindu-Muslim unity across caste and creed.
Analyse the rebels' attack on symbols of oppression and their attempts to set up an alternative structure of power.
State the special laws passed by the British in 1857 to suppress the rebellion.
Explain why the British reconquest of Delhi and the Gangetic plain was slow and difficult.
Explain how the British used promises of land to break the unity of landholders and peasants.
Interpret how British paintings, cartoons and prints celebrated saviours and justified vengeance and repression.
Explain how nationalist art and literature presented 1857 and its leaders.

chapters.title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: Civil Disobedience and Beyond

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Gandhiji's years in South Africa and the India of 1915 shaped his entry into Indian politics.
Explain why Gandhiji's Banaras Hindu University speech of February 1916 was both a statement of fact and a statement of intent.

topics.title: The Making and Unmaking of Non-cooperation

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how the localised struggles of 1917-18 and the Rowlatt Satyagraha made Gandhiji a national leader.
Explain the aims of Non-cooperation and the reasons for joining it with the Khilafat Movement.
Analyse why Gandhiji called off Non-cooperation after the Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922.
Explain how Gandhiji's dress and the charkha helped him identify with the labouring poor.
Interpret what the rumours about Gandhiji's powers reveal about how peasants saw him.
Describe how Congress organisation, followers and supporters broadened Gandhian nationalism.

topics.title: The Salt Satyagraha: Purna Swaraj and Dandi

concepts.learning_objective: State the significance of the Lahore Congress of 1929 and the observance of Independence Day in 1930.
Explain why Gandhiji chose the salt monopoly as the target of the Dandi March.
Compare the wider streams of protest during Civil Disobedience with those of Non-cooperation.

topics.title: Dialogues: Round Table Conferences and Separate Electorates

concepts.learning_objective: State why the Salt March was a notable event in the national movement.
Explain the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and why the Round Table dialogues remained inconclusive.
Compare the views of Gandhiji and Ambedkar on separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.

topics.title: Quit India and the Last Heroic Days

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the failure of the Cripps Mission and the mass character of the Quit India Movement.
Explain how the 1946 elections and Direct Action Day led to political polarisation and Partition.
Evaluate Gandhiji's work for communal harmony after Independence and the response to his death.

topics.title: Knowing Gandhi: Sources for the Nationalist Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse what private letters and autobiographies reveal and the care needed in reading them.
Interpret the Fortnightly Reports of the Home Department as a colonial source.
Explain why contemporary newspapers are useful but not unprejudiced sources.

chapters.title: Framing the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era

topics.title: A Tumultuous Time and the Making of the Constituent Assembly

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the political situation of 1945-47, including popular upsurges, Partition violence and the problem of the princely states, in which the Constituent Assembly met.
Explain how the members of the Constituent Assembly were chosen and why the Congress dominated it.
Identify the roles played by Nehru, Patel, Rajendra Prasad and Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly.
Recognise the members of the Drafting Committee and the civil servants who assisted the framing of the Constitution.

topics.title: The Vision of the Constitution: The Objectives Resolution

concepts.learning_objective: State the ideals proclaimed in the Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946.
Interpret Nehru's argument that India would learn from other revolutions and democracies without merely copying them.
Explain Somnath Lahiri's criticism that the Constituent Assembly worked under the shadow of British power.
Explain Nehru's claim that the Assembly drew its strength from the will of the people and the social struggles behind it.
Distinguish the colonial Acts of 1909, 1919 and 1935 from the constitution-making of 1946-49.

topics.title: Defining Rights: The Problem with Separate Electorates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe B. Pocker Bahadur's case for continuing separate electorates for Muslims.
Analyse the arguments of Patel, Pant and others against separate electorates and their concern for a unified nation.

topics.title: Protection for the Poor, Tribals and Depressed Castes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain N.G. Ranga's view that the real minorities were the poor and downtrodden masses.
Describe Jaipal Singh's arguments for protecting tribals through reservation of seats.
Explain the demands of Depressed Caste members and the measures finally recommended by the Assembly.
Describe the three lists of subjects, Article 356 and the fiscal provisions of the Constitution.
Explain K. Santhanam's arguments for giving greater powers to the provinces.
Analyse why most members, especially after Partition, argued for a strong Centre.

topics.title: The Language of the Nation, Universal Franchise and Secularism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Mahatma Gandhi wanted Hindustani, a composite language, to be the national language.
Describe the Hindi debate, the fears of non-Hindi speakers and the Language Committee's compromise formula.
Evaluate universal adult franchise and the Indian idea of secularism as features of the Constitution.
